data.say:
Fixes made (2): **p10** — “silent and bowed by the wall” misread 壁によってうつむきながら; amended to “leaning against the wall, silent and with head bowed”. **p26–p27** — the flat “something great” dropped なにか大きな希み; amended to “some great hope, a hope she herself did not understand and yet a great hope”, keeping her inarticulacy and the repetition.

No other sense, continuity, or crux faults found: the potato stays physical and uninterpreted, the phantom picture stays a picture seen from far off in flat, repeated diction, “that day” and the three people stay unidentified, “only three years” / “just a little longer” stay unexalted, and the frame closes on the bare “A storm,” unchanged in kind.

**Verdict: ready** — after the two fixes above, the English says what the Japanese says, holds the expansion and contraction around p10–p16 in one voice, and keeps Bōya, the smile/far/all/long repetitions, and the last line plain.

House log: Final read fixed two sense slips (wall posture p10, “hope” p26–p27) and otherwise passed the text as ready, crux and storm-frame intact.
